name: Pulp
hook: Jarvis Cocker started the band as a schoolboy in Sheffield and spent fifteen years turning it into Britpop's sharpest class commentary.

blurb.age7: Pulp were a band from Sheffield led by Jarvis Cocker, who wrote clever, funny songs about ordinary people's lives.
blurb.age13: Jarvis Cocker started Pulp while still at school in Sheffield in 1978, but the band didn't become famous until the mid-1990s, when 'Common People' (1995) turned a sharp, specific story about class tourism into one of the era's biggest hits. Critics have often compared Cocker's witty, observational songwriting to the Kinks' Ray Davies.
blurb.adult: Pulp's fifteen-plus-year gap between formation and success is unusual even by British music's standards, and it shaped Cocker's songwriting into something more specific and class-conscious than most of his Britpop peers. Critics reaching for a comparison for Cocker's persona and lyrical eye have repeatedly landed on Ray Davies, framing Pulp (in one widely repeated line) as "the Kinks" to Blur and Oasis's Beatles and Stones.

signatureTracks.title: Common People
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: A specific, class-conscious narrative built the way a Kinks song is built: one character, one situation, observed closely rather than generalized.

signatureTracks.title: Disco 2000
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The other half of Pulp's commercial peak, trading "Common People"'s anger for wistful, very English nostalgia.
